required_outcomes: Treats the fence as a separate matter from the oven request: logs it as its own request (or records it for separate handling) rather than adding it to the oven job or to Lantern Works' instruction.

Replies to the tenant honestly: no earlier record of the fence report was found, it has now been logged, and what happens next (landlord asked, or details requested), without inventing a visit date or contractor.
Starts the fence's own path: asks the landlord whether to send a fencing or garden contractor, or asks the tenant for a photo and the details needed to instruct one.
Leaves the oven job on its current track with Lantern Works (returned to auto mode or otherwise unchanged).
acceptable_alternatives: Asking the tenant for a photo and whether the panel is on a boundary shared with a neighbour before raising it with the landlord, provided the fence is recorded so it is not lost.
Telling the tenant the fence will be handled under a separate request and raising it with the landlord in the same step.
positive_behaviours: Asks whether the leaning panel is a risk (could fall on someone, children or pets in the garden) and suggests keeping clear of it meanwhile.
Notes that the July phone report was apparently never logged, so the gap is visible to the team.
red_flags: Telling the tenant the fence is booked, in hand or about to be repaired when nothing on record supports it.
Escalating a routine fence question to a human.
prohibited_actions: Assigning Lantern Works (the appliance repair provider) to the fence.
Approving spend for fence work without the landlord's approval.
critical_failures: Ignoring the fence question: no reply to the tenant about it and no record of it anywhere.
